items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: I played with him much later

ctx.x: All right, so after the Arabee, it seems the band broke up and like you mentioned, Charlie Echols. Charlie Echols was the west coast's Cab Calloway. Charles Echols. He used to get a lot of gigs -- but he always wanted the best musicians. He could not play a note, but he stood in front of the band like Cab and he would sing these songs and he would conduct the band and shake his head because he imitated Cab, really, but not -- he couldn't scat and all that, but I mean he was the west coast's Cab Calloway, and he…

I played with him much later, but you know, at this point in time, I didn't work with him yet, but it seems to me after Buck Clayton, I really started getting my recognition, you know, at Stuff Smith came out ... I know this is in '37-- Stuff Smith came out, oh, let's see ... no, I got to go back.
